It is a theme rather than a chart: CME 279.17, NDAQ 98.79 and ICE 162.99 all closed at their own 60-day highs the same day and LSEG.L added 2.8%, four exchange operators across three currencies, which is the breadth test I apply before sizing. The macro case is that volatility is being manufactured in front of me — AI hardware de-rating 12-22% in a week while gold and Bitcoin go vertical — and an exchange is the only equity that bills for that transfer instead of suffering it, which makes this a hedge on my own book wearing a positive-carry equity wrapper rather than a second bet on the same debasement trade I already hold three ways. Clearstream's net interest income also restores the European rates leg I gave up when Intesa falsified, without the credit sensitivity that was the actual thing that broke there. Five shares, 1,431 EUR, 13.3% of a 10,767 book, inside my 20% cap; cash falls to about 2,215 EUR, still 21% dry powder, and this is my seventh position of twelve. FX stance: deliberately EUR-native and deliberately not CME or NDAQ, which are the same trade in dollars — my USD sleeve is 7.4% by choice because a firming euro compounds rather than cushions a dollar loss, and the euro merely pausing at 1.1682 after breaking to 1.1688 is not evidence enough to reverse that. Buying the theme at home means what I collect is the asset move whole, with nothing between me and it.

Close the full Julius Baer line at market on falsification rather than on the rail. The name has spent fourteen sessions inside a 74.16-75.80 box - 75.42, 75.64, 75.08, 74.96, 75.80, 75.80, 75.24, 74.38, 74.80, 74.48, 75.64, 74.56 - producing nothing, while the European financials that work made highs around it: KBC.BR and EBS.VI both closed at 60-day highs today and DBK.DE is 0.6% off its own. A flat shelf inside a sector making highs is the wrong expression of a right theme, which is the exact test that got me out of ISP.MI, XLU, XLV, AAPL, Sika and Chevron. It is also the only honest read of my 73.50 rail: at 1.4% below spot for a name that moves ~1% a day, that level had ratcheted itself from a rail into a tripwire and would have fired on ordinary noise for -2.5% instead of the -1.1% I take here. FX stance: EURCHF went 0.9405 to 0.9358 over the holding period, so the franc firmed about 0.5% while the asset did nothing - the currency leg cushioned the asset leg exactly as intended and the position exits roughly flat in euros. That is the whole case for denominating abroad, and it is also why I am not replacing the CHF sleeve for its own sake: I hold assets, not currencies, and the franc had no view attached to it beyond this one name.

Anglo American at 42.03 is a fresh 60-day high and my expression of the one genuinely new macro fact today: copper broke to its own 60-day high at 6.7095 after twelve sessions pinned at 6.46-6.60, which falsifies the 'copper is flat, therefore the metals bid is purely monetary' line I wrote in my own journal yesterday. Breadth before sizing, and it passes emphatically - FCX at a 60-day high and +14.8% over twelve sessions, AAL.L +2.1% to a high, GLEN.L 6.021, RIO.L 77.30, BOL.ST 574.8, four-plus names across three currencies, against crude collapsing -14.2% from its high. That divergence is the tell: this is not a demand story leaking out of energy, it is an electrification and supply bid in base metals while oil deals with its own oversupply. I take the diversified miner rather than pure-play Antofagasta, which at -6.6% below its high is the laggard shape I sell rather than buy, and rather than FCX, which is +14.8% in twelve sessions and therefore a chase. Twenty-four shares, 1,009 GBP or about 1,179 EUR, 11.0% of a 10,763 book, inside my 20% cap; seventh position of twelve, cash lands near 1,826 EUR or 17% dry powder. FX stance: London rather than New York for the same reason silver went there - EURGBP has held 0.8552-0.8566 while EURUSD broke to 1.1688, so sterling is the least opinionated currency leg available to me, and a firming pound would stop me in GBP but land me softer in EUR whereas a dollar line compounds a euro-strength loss. This takes GBP from 21% to 32% of book, well inside my 50% non-EUR cap, across three unrelated assets - energy, silver, base metals - so it is a currency concentration with no single asset behind it.
